info.title: Dameless
info.description: You and your engine, getting stronger at one board. Every command of the `dameless` CLI is one of these routes. Every request but `/api/health` carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

post.summary: Deletes the binaries nothing uses: every version's older builds, or all of them with `keep_latest: false`.

delete.summary: Deletes a build's binary; its record stays for what used it. 409 while something uses it.

get.summary: Profiles side by side, with who leads each row.
Both Lichess connections as the app shows them.
The bots online on Lichess now, with their ratings.

post.summary:
Takes the bot online (it stays online across restarts until taken offline) or offline (games in progress are
played out).

The bot looks for games against other bots: `once` until one starts, `always` after every game too, `off` stops
(and withdraws the challenge waiting for an answer).

put.summary:
Replaces the bot's settings: the version it plays, hash, threads, move overhead, which challenges it takes, and
how it seeks. Answers the settings as stored.

post.summary:
Starts logging in to your Lichess account (OAuth with PKCE): open the link. Lichess sends the browser back to the
app's callback, which stores the token and sends the browser on to `return_to` with `?lichess=connected` (or
`?lichess=error&message=…`). The link works once, for ten minutes.
Opens a seek in the lobby for you (rapid or slower, the Board API's rule). The game starts when someone takes it.

delete.summary: Logs a connection out: forgets its token (revoking yours at Lichess). Games in progress go on at Lichess.

post.summary:
Challenges from a connection: yours to a player (blitz or slower), Lichess's AI (`ai_level`) or your bot
(`my_bot`); the bot's to a player (the bot must be online).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: `you` (the bot answers challenges by its settings).

post.summary:
Accepts a challenge to you; the game starts on the event stream. 400 for one the Board API cannot play (bullet,
variants): accept that on lichess.org.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: `you` (the bot answers challenges by its settings).

post.summary: Declines a challenge to you.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: `you` (the bot answers challenges by its settings).

put.summary:
Stores a Lichess token after Lichess checks it. Yours must be a person's account allowed to play; the bot's a
BOT account. Neither may be the other's.

get.summary: Dameless's logbook: champion, line, ideas, the bot and its strength over versions.

post.summary: Pushes the fork's `main` to `origin`. Only ever on this explicit request (the UI confirms first).

get.summary: Every dataset, the cap on them together and the room left.

post.summary:
Self-play data with Reckless's datagen branch (work). The same name again grows that dataset. 409 when the cap or
the disk leaves no room.

Downloads one shard into a dataset (work). Refused (400) without `confirm: true` for the size shown; 409 when the
download and its conversion would pass the cap or fill the disk.

delete.summary: Deletes a dataset's files. 400 without `confirm: true`; 409 while something uses it.

get.summary:
The machine's health for Settings: fastchess, the book, the engine checkout, clang, CUDA, the GPU, the disk, the
database, builds and the harness check, each with what to do about it.
Every drill, soonest due first.

post.summary: Makes drills from your profile's weak spots (new positions only); answers the drills made.

get.summary:
Today's drills: due ones first, then new ones up to the day's cap. Show only `fen`, `side` and `theme` before
the answer.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many in all (default 30).

get.summary: Your drill hit rate over time, a point per day with a rolling mean (window 50 answers).

post.summary: Answers a drill (UCI or SAN): the outcome, the drill rescheduled, and the answer with its line.

get.summary: The evaluation sessions running now. A session that reached its budget is no longer listed.

post.summary:
Starts a live search. Its progress comes as `eval.info` events on topic `eval:<session>`; it ends at its budget,
when stopped, or when the policy turns analysis off.

delete.summary: Stops a session and waits until its engine has stopped.

get.summary: The live event stream.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Replay the kept events after this id. `Last-Event-ID` does the same for a reconnecting browser.

parameters.name: topics
parameters.description: Topics, comma-separated (`games,game:12,work`, `game:*`). None: every topic but `eval:*` and game detail.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: The API token, for clients that cannot send headers (`EventSource`).

get.summary:
Lichess's opening explorer, as Lichess answers it. Needs your Lichess login (409 without it); refused while you
play on Lichess unless every game of yours is correspondence.

parameters.name: fen
parameters.description: The position as FEN; the start position when none.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: From this month (`2020-01`), or year for `masters`.

get.summary: Games, live ones first in the list's order of newest first.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Games started at or after this time (ISO-8601).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: The page after this game (the last id of the previous page).

parameters.name: calibration
parameters.description: Calibration games between levels: left out unless `true` (only them) or `all`.

post.summary:
Starts a local game: you against Dameless, or Dameless against itself. Engines are started (their versions built
when needed) before the game is stored.

Stores pasted PGN as finished local games (one per game in the text). A player is you when `you` says so or the
tag names your Lichess account; anyone else is kept as a Lichess player of that name.

get.summary: A game as it is now: a live game's clocks, offers and your actions laid over the stored record.

post.summary:
Does an action as you in a game you play: 409 when the game is over or the action is not one of `Game.actions`
now, 400 for a move that is not legal. A move answers once it is on the board.

get.summary: A game as PGN, with a comment on every move (eval/depth, think time, nodes, clock).
A game's newest review (or the one with this version and budget). 404 without one.

parameters.name: version
parameters.description: The version that reviewed it (`champion`, `v14`, `#12`, a branch); the newest review when none.

parameters.name: nodes
parameters.description: The node budget per position; any when none.

post.summary:
Stops a live game: a game you sit in is resigned (aborted before each side has moved), an engine game aborted,
the bot's resigned on Lichess. Answers the game once it has ended, or as it stands after a few seconds.

get.summary: Whether this machine's harness is trusted: the last check, whether it still applies, and one running.

post.summary:
Starts a harness check: `main` against a branch identical to it at VSTC [0, 3] (which must reject it), and with
`pairs`, a symmetry run of that many pairs. Answers its idea. 409 while one runs or without fastchess and the book.

get.summary: Whether the app is up. The one route that needs no token.
Ideas, newest first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: At most this many, newest first; all when none.

post.summary:
Creates an idea and queues its first trial. A `custom` trial instead of the funnel is a single test (any preset,
bounds or a fixed number of pairs). A branch whose `Bench:` line is missing or stale is refused (409) unless
`fix_bench` asks for it to be fixed.
Several ideas under one tag, all checked before any is queued; they run one after another.

get.summary: Whether a branch's tip has a right `Bench:` line (ok, missing, stale, or not built yet to tell). Never builds.

post.summary:
Builds a branch's tip if needed and rewords it with the measured `Bench:` line (locally, never pushed). 409 when
the branch moved since `commit`; 400 for `main` or upstream.

get.summary: An idea with its trials.

post.summary: A dataset made from an idea's trial games. 404 without trial games.

Promotes a kept idea: its branch is merged into the fork's `main` locally, making the next champion, which is the
answer. Refused (409, nothing changed) when the checkout has uncommitted changes. Pushing is separate.
Carries on a stopped or failed idea from the trial that did not finish.
Stops an idea: its running trial at the next safe point (keeping its rounds), or a queued one at once.

get.summary: A net idea's training: its settings, every reading (resumes included) and the net it made. 404 for another kind.
One trial of an idea, with its evidence.

A tune idea's settings, its parameters and its SPSA history (one step per update). 404 for an idea that is not a
tune.
The ladder of levels with their calibrated ratings, your rating on it and the level suggested for you.

post.summary:
Queues calibration (background work at the lowest priority): levels play each other at fixed nodes, and the
ladder is refitted after each match.

get.summary: The calibration matches that would teach the most now: neighbouring levels, the widest and most even first.
Every net the app knows, newest first.
One net.
Lichess's leaderboard at a speed.

Your repertoire with one colour, from your games: the lines you play, where you leave theory, how you score.
Refused (409) while you play on Lichess, unless every game of yours is correspondence.

parameters.name: max_plies
parameters.description: How deep the tree goes, in plies (20).

parameters.name: min_games
parameters.description: A move shows once played in this many games (2).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Your newest finished games read, at most (500).

get.summary: What is known of a player.

post.summary:
Imports a player's finished games from Lichess (work, network only): `you` (your history, needs your login) or
`lichess:<name>` (theirs; refused while you play on Lichess).

get.summary:
A player's games added up: results over every finished game, engine figures over the reviewed ones, weak spots
for you.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: Only games from this time on (ISO-8601, or a date).

get.summary: Both players' lines: your rating, accuracy and drill hit rate, and Dameless's Elo over its versions.

post.summary: Queues a review (work). Refused while you play on Lichess; a running review pauses while you do.
Downloads fastchess and the opening book the trials use into the tools folder. Only on this explicit request.

get.summary: The status line's facts, and Settings › Machine.
The tablebase's answer for a position of seven pieces or fewer, as Lichess gives it. Refused while you play.

parameters.name: fen
parameters.description: A position with at most seven pieces.

get.summary: The API token, for pairing the hosted UI with this app (Settings shows it to copy).

post.summary: A training run outside any idea (work on the GPU). 409 without a GPU; 404 for an unknown parent net or dataset.

get.summary:
The tunables a branch declares (`src/parameters.rs`), read from its `spsa` build. When that build is not there
yet, it is queued and the answer is 409: ask again once it is done (`GET /api/work`).

parameters.name: branch
parameters.description: The branch (or any version) whose tunables to list.

get.summary: Versions, newest first.

post.summary: Makes a version of a branch, tag or commit and queues its build (see `GET /api/work`). Answers the version.

get.summary: A version's builds, newest first (diagnostics).
Work running, queued and recently finished.
One work item.
A work item's log, as plain text. Lines also come live as `work.log` events.

post.summary: Pauses an item until it is resumed: a running one at its next safe point, a queued one is held.
Carries on paused work.
Stops an item: a queued one at once, a running one at its next safe point.

get.summary: One run's readings.

Account.description: A Lichess account as a connection knows it.

ActionBody.description: The body of an action; only `move` needs one.

Assist.description:
How much assistance is allowed now. Lichess forbids engines, books and tablebases during a game; its explorer is
allowed in correspondence only.

BotSettings.description:
The bot's settings: what plays, how, and which challenges it accepts. Stored by `play`; old or partial stored
settings fill in the defaults.

from_position.description: Also accept standard chess from a set position (Lichess's `fromPosition`). Other variants are always declined.

hash.description: Hash table size in MiB. Default 64.

max_games.description: Games at once. Challenges beyond this are declined as `later`. Default 1.

max_increment.description: The largest increment accepted, in seconds.

max_initial.description: The longest initial clock accepted, in seconds.

min_increment.description: The smallest increment accepted, in seconds.

min_initial.description: The shortest initial clock accepted, in seconds.

move_overhead.description:
Milliseconds the engine keeps in hand on every move for the network, as Reckless's `MoveOverhead` (0 to 2000).
Default 300.

seek_clocks.description:
The clocks the bot challenges other bots at when it looks for a game, as Lichess writes them: minutes plus
increment seconds, such as `3+2`. One is picked at random for each challenge. Default 3+0, 3+2 and 5+3.

seek_range.description:
The rating window for opponents when looking for a game: bots within this many points of ours at that speed
are preferred, then within twice as many, then any. Default 300.

seek_rated.description: Whether the challenges it sends when looking for a game are rated. Default true.

speeds.description: The speeds accepted. UltraBullet and correspondence are never played.

version.description:
The version that plays: a version name such as `v14` or an id, or `champion` meaning the champion at the start
of each game. Nothing plays (challenges are declined) until one is chosen.

BotStatus.description: What only the bot's connection has.

bot_games_today.description: Games against bots started in the last 24 hours.

oneOf.description: While at the daily limit: when it lifts.

BranchCheck.description: `GET /api/ideas/check-branch?branch=`: a branch's tip and its `Bench:` line.

measured.description: What its build measured, when it has been built.

oneOf.description: Until stopped (the board's engine switch).

Build.description: A binary of a version: a cache keyed by commit, cargo features and net, shown in diagnostics only.

bench.description: What its `bench` measured: must equal the commit's `Bench:` line.

features.description: Cargo features it was built with, such as `spsa`.

oneOf.description: The net it embeds, when not the commit's own.

nps.description: Nodes per second of a single `bench`.

BuildId.description: One binary of a version (a cache keyed by commit and features).

count.description: How many planned matches, when `matches` is not given. Default 3.

games_per_pair.description: Games per match, overriding each match's own (`core::levels::CALIBRATION_GAMES`, 20).

matches.description: These matches; else the plan's `count` most useful ones.

version.description: The version every level plays; the champion when none.

Challenge.description: A challenge to or from one of the connections.

color.description: The colour the connection would play.

id.description: Lichess's id, which becomes the game's id when accepted.

playable.description: Whether this app can play it (the Board API cannot play bullet or variants).

oneOf.description: None for unlimited games.

ChallengeBody.description:
`POST /api/connections/{key}/challenge`: exactly one of `username`, `ai_level` (yours only) and `my_bot` (yours
only).

ChallengeEvent.description: The `challenge` event: what became of a challenge, with Lichess's decline key and a few words more.

id.description: The challenge id, which becomes the game's when accepted (an AI game's id at once).

ClassCounts.description: How many moves got each classification.

Classification.description: What a review calls a move.

Color.description: A colour chosen when starting a game or a challenge: a side, or let chance decide.

confirm.description: Your explicit go-ahead: deleting a dataset cannot be undone.

ConnectionKey.description: A Lichess account linked to the app: yours, or Dameless's BOT account.

ConnectionStatus.description: A connection as the app shows it: the `connection.upserted` event and `GET /api/connections`.

playing.description: Games being played here through this connection.

CustomTrial.description: A custom idea's single trial (what `chess test` was).

bounds.description: SPRT bounds in normalized Elo; with neither these nor `pairs`, [0, 3].

pairs.description: A fixed number of game pairs instead of an SPRT.

oneOf.description: The bot, when its Lichess account is connected.

strength.description:
Each champion version and its cumulative Elo over `v1` (each promotion's deciding estimate added up, the
errors in quadrature), oldest first.

DataStatus.description: `GET /api/datasets`: every dataset, and the room left.

cap_bytes.description: The cap on every dataset together (`DAMELESS_DATA_CAP_GB`).

disk_free_bytes.description: Free space on the data directory's disk.

keep_free_bytes.description: What training work always leaves free.

name.description: The dataset to write or grow; `datagen` when left out. Running again on the same name resumes it.

positions.description: The dataset's total positions to reach (positions already there count).

soft_nodes.description: Soft nodes per move (the tool's default, 5,000, when left out).

threads.description: Worker threads (one engine each); half the machine's cores when left out, at most what the ledger grants.

version.description: The engine: a version of Reckless's datagen branch (`origin/datagen` when left out).

Dataset.description: A dataset: a directory with a `manifest.json`.

name.description: Unique: also its directory's name under the data directory's `data/`.

score_units.description: `cp` or `reckless_internal`; training wants Reckless's internal units.

DatasetId.description: A dataset directory the app knows.

oneOf.description: Self-play with Reckless's `datagen` branch; `settings` as the tool recorded them.
A shard downloaded (with your go-ahead) and converted.
An idea's trial games, converted.
Anything else the manifest names.

Departure.description: Where a game first left theory, added up over the games that left at the same move.

by_you.description: You left theory, rather than your opponent.

example.description: The newest such game, to open on the board.

key.description: The last position in theory, and the move that left it.

score.description: Your points per game in those games, 0 to 1.

Drill.description: One drill and where its schedule stands.

oneOf.description: The last answer; `None` for a drill never tried (a new one).

best_moves.description: Every move that counts as correct (UCI), the engine's best first: all within [`CORRECT_WITHIN`] of it.

best_san.description: The same in SAN, for the answer.

due.description: When it is next due, and the interval that set it.

fen.description: The position to find a move in, and its key (the FEN without move counters), which drills are unique by.

game.description: The game and ply the mistake was made at.

line.description: The engine's line after its best move (UCI), shown with the answer.

played.description: What you played in the game, UCI and SAN.

reps.description: Passes in a row, and misses in all.

swing.description: Win percentage lost in the game.

DrillAnswerResult.description: What an answer came to: the outcome, the drill rescheduled, and the answer itself.

DrillAnswered.description: `drill.answered`: a drill was answered; the rescheduled drill follows as `drill.upserted`.

drills.description: In the order to play them. The client shows `fen`, `side` and `theme` only until the drill is answered.

due.description: How many of them are tried drills due again, and how many new.

started_today.description: New drills started today, counted against the day's cap.

ElsewhereGame.description: A game of yours on Lichess that cannot be played here (bullet, a variant): it still turns analysis off.

branch.description: The branch checked out, if any.

dirty.description: Uncommitted changes (they block promoting into a checked-out `main`).

found.description: Whether it is a git checkout.

EntrantRating.description: An entrant's fitted rating: the estimate with its 95 % interval, and the games it rests on.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every error answer: `{ "error": { "code": "conflict", "message": "…" } }`.

ErrorCode.description: The codes errors carry in the API's `{ error: { code, message } }`.

Estimate.description: An estimate with its 95 % interval: `elo` and the interval's ends.

EvalBody.description: `POST /api/eval`: a live search of a position.

client.description: Who asks (a browser tab, a CLI run): one session per client, a new one replaces the old.

fen.description: The start position as FEN; none for the standard start.

moves.description: Moves from it, UCI or SAN.

version.description: The version to search with (`champion`, `v14`, `#12`, a branch); the champion when none.

EvalLine.description: One line of a live evaluation. `score` is White's.

EvalSession.description: A started session: its events come on topic `eval:<session>`.

fen.description: The position searched, after the moves.

id.description: Monotonic; pass the last one seen as `since` (or `Last-Event-ID`) to resume. 0 on `reload`.

Event.description:
One event of the stream, as each `data:` line carries it: `{ id, topic, kind, data }`, where `kind` names the
payload's type. Every score in a payload is White's.

oneOf.description: At most five a second, never replayed.

data.description: At most five a second, never replayed.

oneOf.description: Never replayed.
Never replayed.
Not a domain event: the stream has a hole, so fetch what is shown again.

data.description: Not a domain event: the stream has a hole, so fetch what is shown again.

FixBenchRequest.description:
`POST /api/ideas/fix-bench`: the branch to fix, and optionally the tip it was checked at, so a branch that moved
since is not reworded blind.

Game.description: The full record of a game.

actions.description: What You may do now; anything else is refused.

oneOf.description: While live: the clock each side holds now, in ms.

start_fen.description: The start position; none for the standard start.

GameChanged.description: `game.changed`: offers, what You may do, the clocks or the opponent's presence changed.

GameId.description: A game: played here, on Lichess, imported, or a trial's.

GameSummary.description: What lists, events and the Games rail show of a game.

oneOf.description: Each side's accuracy from the newest review.
The side You played, if any.

GameThinking.description: `game.thinking`: the engine to move's progress. `score` is White's.

ply.description: The ply being chosen, so a late report for a move already played can be dropped.

GameUndone.description: `game.undone`: moves were taken back; `plies` is how many are left.

HarnessCheck.description: A finished check, as stored for the machine (`meta` key `harness.check`).

oneOf.description: Logistic Elo of the identical engine ± 95 %.

engine_commit.description: The champion's commit it was played with.

pairs.description: Also play this many pairs for the symmetry check (the UI offers 2,000); none skips it.

HarnessStatus.description:
`GET /api/harness`: whether results on this machine can be trusted. Trials' verdicts show `summary` beside them
while `trusted` is false.

checked.description: A check has finished on some machine.

current.description: The last check was on this machine, with the fastchess and book installed now.

oneOf.description: The last check, in full.
A check queued or running now.

trusted.description: Checked here, current and passed: results on this machine can be trusted.

Health.description: `GET /api/health`: every item, and whether none fails.

HealthAction.description: What fixes an item: a label for the button, and the CLI command that does the same.

ok.description: Not failing (a warning or a note is still ok).

HitRatePoint.description: One day of the hit-rate trend.

rate.description: Passes per answer that day, 0 to 1.

rolling.description: Passes per answer over the last `window` answers up to the end of that day: the line the UI draws.

Idea.description: A hypothesis and a change to try.

base.description: What it is tested against, usually the champion when queued.

branch.description: The change; for a tune, the branch with the tunables.

notes.description: Claude's or your reasoning, in markdown.

verdict.description: One sentence: "Kept: +3.1 ± 2.0 Elo at short games".

oneOf.description: The version under test (a tune's once SPSA has written it).

IdeaId.description: An idea: a hypothesis and a change to try.

IdeaKind.description: What kind of change an idea is, which picks its funnel.

max.description: At most this many games, newest first; all when none.

since.description: Games started at or after this time (ms since 1970). Your history: after the newest imported before.

oneOf.description: The side you played, when not found by your Lichess username in the tags.

ImportRequest.description: `POST /api/datasets/import`: one shard to download, with your go-ahead for its size.

confirm.description: Your explicit go-ahead for downloading `expected_bytes`: without it the request is refused.

expected_bytes.description: The download's size, as shown to you before you confirmed it.

name.description: The dataset it goes into (shards of one set share a name).

sha256.description: Checked after the download, when given.

JudgementCounts.description: Lichess's own counts: misses count as the mistake or blunder they are.

Leader.description: A row of the comparison and who leads it (indexes into the profiles; several on a tie, none without figures).

progress.description: Rating change over the last games.

LedgerSnapshot.description: The ledger as the status line shows it.

free.description: What work can still be granted.

gpu_grants.description: The work holding each GPU in use.

gpus.description: GPUs on the machine (`DAMELESS_GPUS`, else what nvidia-smi finds).

oversubscribed.description: Live play holds more than the machine has, with work on top: games are played anyway, a little slower.

reserved.description: Held by live games and live evaluation.

id.description: 1 is the weakest; the last level of the ladder is full strength.

multipv.description: Lines searched: the candidates [`choose_move`] picks among. 1 plays the engine's best move.

name.description: `Level 5`; the UI writes "Dameless at 1600" from the calibrated rating.

nodes.description:
Nodes per move. `None` is full strength: the engine plays on the clock, as in any other game (calibration
games give it [`FULL_CALIBRATION_NODES`]).

nominal.description: The rating the level was designed for, until calibration measures it.

temperature.description:
The softmax temperature, in win percentage points (0 to 100) of the side to move: a candidate that many points
worse than the best is chosen `e` times less often. 0 always plays the best move.

oneOf.description: The calibrated rating, once the level has games; else `null` (the UI says "about <nominal>").

suggested.description: The level nearest your rating (fitted, else Lichess's): the New game dialog's default.

oneOf.description: When the last fit was made.
Your fitted rating on the ladder's scale, once there is a fit with you in it.
The fork's `main`, numbered `v1`, `v2`, … in order of promotion.
An idea's change (or a tune's result).
A tip of upstream Reckless.
Anything else built by ref.

Line.description: Which line of development a version is on.

Llr.description: A trial's log-likelihood ratio and the bounds that decide it.

return_to.description: The page to come back to: the app on a loopback address or the hosted UI (default the app's `/you`).

LrSchedule.description: How the learning rate falls over a run, as `bullet-train --lr-schedule` takes it.

Machine.description: The machine a check ran on.

cpu.description: The CPU's brand string, "Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10700K CPU @ 3.80GHz".

limit.description: At most this many new drills (20 when none).

ref.description: A branch, tag or commit of the fork (or `champion`, `v14`, `#12`).

Moment.description: A move worth linking to: the board opens the game at `ply`.

sacrifice.description: Pawns of material given up (brilliant moves).

url.description: The game on Lichess, at the move.

Moments.description: The best and worst of a player's reviewed games.

best.description: The brilliant moves with the most material given up (at most 3), else the great ones.

blunders.description: The worst blunders by win percentage lost (at most 3).

clock_ms.description: The mover's clock after the move (increment included).

oneOf.description: The mover's engine's own score, from White's point of view; engines only (and Lichess's analysis on imports).

arch.description: The architecture, [`RECKLESS_ARCH`] for every net so far.

oneOf.description: The (first) dataset it was trained on.

metrics.description: Offline metrics (validation loss, ...), when measured. Not measured yet: always null for now.

name.description: `v60-7f587dfb` for a shipped net, the run's name for a trained one (`net-3`).

oneOf.description: The net it was fine-tuned from.

path.description: The file in the data directory's `nets/`, absolute.

oneOf.description: The run that made it; none for a shipped net.

NetId.description: A network file the app knows.

NetRun.description: The training run a net came from.

oneOf.description: The idea it was trained for, when it was.

positions.description: Positions trained on (bullet's count, the dataset cycled).

oneOf.description: The `Train` work item.

adjudicate.description: End decided games early, as the trials do (engines' scores only).

seed.description: Seeds the choices of seats at a level, so a game can be replayed; random when none.

base.description: What it is tested against: a version (`v14`, a branch, `#12`); the champion when left out.

branch.description: The change: a branch of the fork (for a tune, the branch with the tunables).

oneOf.description: One trial with any preset and bounds or a fixed number of pairs, instead of the funnel.

fix_bench.description:
When the branch's tip has no `Bench:` line or a stale one, build it and reword the tip with the measured bench
before creating the idea (this changes the fork's branch locally). Without it, such a branch is refused with a
409, since the fingerprint stage would fail on it.

long.description: Add the long-games stage to the funnel.

oneOf.description:
A net idea's training run (a fine-tune of its base's net with the default schedule when left out). A net idea
needs no branch: it trains for the champion's code (`branch` may be left empty).
A tune's settings (a tune idea without them tunes with OpenBench's defaults).

Offers.description: Offers standing in a live game: who offered a draw, who asked to take back.

OnlineBot.description: A bot online now, as `GET /api/bot/online` lists it.

Opening.description: The opening as Lichess names it.

ply.description: How many plies the named opening covers: moves up to it are `book` in a review.

name.description: The opening family as Lichess names it, without the ECO code or the variation ("Sicilian Defense").

Opponent.description: Someone on the other side of a challenge.

OpponentGone.description: The opponent left a Lichess game.

claim_in_seconds.description: Seconds until a claim may be made.

average_rating.description: The opponents' average rating, over the decided games where it is known.

performance.description: A simple performance rating: the opponents' average plus 400 × (wins − losses) / games.

Pentanomial.description: Game-pair outcomes from the dev engine's side: `[LL, LD, WL+DD, WD, WW]`, i.e. pairs scoring 0, ½, 1, 1½ and 2.

PhaseReview.description: One side's play in one phase.

accuracy.description: Lichess's game accuracy over this phase's moves, as lila's `phaseAccuracies`.

timed_moves.description: Moves with a known think time (games with a clock, after the first move of each side), and their total.

PhaseStats.description: Average game accuracy (each reviewed game counts once), overall, per phase and per speed.

PlannedMatch.description: A calibration match to play next.

a.description: The two levels, the weaker first.

priority.description:
How much the match is expected to narrow the ladder's intervals, relative to the others: the higher, the
sooner.

Player.description: Someone who sits at a board.

ratings.description: Lichess's ratings per speed, when known.

Policy.description: The fair-play policy, computed from the you connection.

reason.description: Why, while not `allowed`: "Analysis is off while you're playing on Lichess".

Preset.description: Named game settings, as Reckless names its tests.

Priority.description:
Which work runs first when cores are short: the lower, the sooner. Live games and live evaluation reserve their
cores outside the queue; these order the work items.

counts.description: Classifications in all reviewed games, and per game.

games.description: Games considered, of them reviewed, and the rest.

judgements.description: Lichess's own counts (a miss counts as its mistake or blunder).

openings.description: The most played opening families, at most 8.

rating.description: The rating in the newest game considered.

weak_spots.description: Positions from the player's mistakes, recurring themes first; filled for You only.

ProfileFilter.description: Which games a profile adds up.

oneOf.description: Only games from this moment on.

speeds.description: Only these speeds; empty for all.

Progress.description: How far along a piece of work is.

text.description: One sentence for people: "412 pairs, LLR 1.2 of 2.94".

oneOf.description: The game or version the point comes from, to open it.

low.description: A 95 % interval, where the value has one (Dameless's Elo).

dry_run.description: Say what would go, delete nothing.

keep_latest.description: Keep every version's newest build of each feature set (default true).

older_than_days.description: Only binaries at least this old.

builds.description: The builds whose binaries were deleted (or would be).

in_use.description: Builds left alone because something uses them.

head.description: The commit `main` is at, there and here.

provisional.description: Lichess calls a rating provisional until it has settled (`prov`).

Ratings.description: Lichess's ratings per speed, when known.

departures.description: Where games left theory, the most common first (empty without a theory predicate).

nodes.description: The start position first, then by ply and by games.

RepertoireMove.description: A move from a position, with the games that played it and how you scored after it.

leaves_theory.description: The position it leads to is out of theory while this one was in (`None` without a theory predicate).

next.description: The key of the position it leads to.

score.description: Your points per game after it, 0 to 1.

ply.description: The fewest plies it was reached in.

theory.description: Whether it is theory (`None` without a theory predicate).

your_turn.description: Whether you are to move here: then `moves` are your choices, else what you met.

RepertoireOptions.description: How deep and how wide the tree is.

max_plies.description: Plies from the start read into the tree.

min_games.description: Moves (and positions) seen in fewer games are left out, the start position aside.

Review.description: A stored review: the summary and every move.

ReviewBody.description: `POST /api/reviews`: some games, or a player's newest games not reviewed yet with this version and budget.

concurrency.description: Engines at once; half the machine's cores when none.

limit.description: How many of the player's games; 20 when none.

oneOf.description: This player's newest finished games not yet reviewed: `you`, `dameless`, `lichess:<name>`.

version.description: The version to review with (`champion`, `v14`, `#12`, a branch); the champion when none.

middlegame_ply.description: The ply whose move starts the middlegame and the endgame (1 = the first move), when the game got there.

ReviewUpserted.description: `review.upserted`: a game was reviewed; fetch the review for detail.

ReviewedMove.description:
One move as the review judged it. Scores are White's (`{cp}` or `{mate}`; `mate: 0` is the side to move
checkmated, after the game's last move); win percentages and accuracy are the mover's.

accuracy.description: Lichess's accuracy of this move, 0 to 100.

best_uci.description: The engine's best move here, and its line (at most 8 moves, UCI).

clock_before_ms.description: The mover's clock before the move, in a game with a clock.

cp_loss.description: Centipawns lost, each score capped at ±1000.

depth.description: The depth of the search of the position before the move.

eval_after.description: The engine's best score after it.

eval_before.description: The engine's best score before the move.

oneOf.description: Lichess's judgement, which a `miss` also carries.

phase.description: The phase of the position the move was played from.

sacrifice.description: Pawns of material given up along the engine's best reply (a brilliant move gives up 2 or more).

second_uci.description: The second-best move and its score, when there was a second legal move.

Scaling.description: How a trial's or a tune's clock was scaled.

base_nps.description: The mean speed of the copies of base's `bench`. A tune has one build, so both are its speed.

copies.description: Copies of `bench` run at once: the games played at once times each game's threads.

dev_nps.description: The mean speed of the copies of dev's `bench`, in nodes per second.

measured_nps.description: The speed the factor comes from: base's, as Reckless's OpenBench scales its tests.

reference_nps.description: The speed the written clock is meant for.

scale.description: `reference_nps / measured_nps`: what the clock's base time and increment were multiplied by.

Score.description:
A score: centipawns, or a forced mate in so many moves. `{"cp": 31}` or `{"mate": -3}`. From White's point of view
unless a function says otherwise; `mate: 0` means the side to move is checkmated, from either point of view.

Seat.description: Someone at a board, as this game knew them.

oneOf.description: The exact binary a Dameless seat played.

name.description: What to show: "You" is shown as the Lichess username when linked; a Dameless seat by its version's name.

oneOf.description: The version a Dameless seat played.

SeatAction.description:
What a seat can do in a game. One set for every game, local or on Lichess; `Game.actions` lists those You may do
now. A move carries its UCI in the request, not here.

SeatRequest.description: `you`, `dameless` (the champion), `dameless:<version>`, and `@<level>` after either Dameless form to play at a level (`dameless@5`). The object `{ player, version?, level? }` reads too.

SeekChallenge.description: The challenge the bot has sent and is waiting on.

id.description: The challenge id, which becomes the game id if it is accepted.

SeekClock.description: A clock to challenge another bot at: the initial time and the increment, in seconds.

SeekMode.description: Whether, and how, the bot is looking for games.

rating.description: Their rating at the challenge's speed.

note.description: A short sentence on how the search last went, for people to read.

oneOf.description: The challenge sent and not answered yet. There is never more than one.

log.description: What it did, line by line.

SidePair_Option_f32.description: One value per side, such as both clocks or both accuracies.

SidePair_f32.description: One value per side, such as both clocks or both accuracies.

SidePair_u64.description: One value per side, such as both clocks or both accuracies.

acpl.description: Average centipawn loss, as Lichess computes it.

time_trouble_blunders.description: Blunders (Lichess's judgement) played with less than a tenth of the starting clock left.

oneOf.description: Played here, or pasted in as PGN.
Played through one of the Lichess connections.
History read from Lichess: `owner` is whose history it is (you, or another player).
A trial's game, read from fastchess's PGN: its trial and its index there.

Speed.description: Lichess's speeds, from its estimate of a game's length (initial + 40 × increment).

oneOf.description: None for games without a speed (movetime or node limits).
A FEN (or `startpos`) and moves played from it (UCI or SAN).
A random line of the opening book the trials use.

StartFrom.description: Where a game starts, when not from the standard position.

Status.description: The app and the machine it runs on.

lichess_url.description: The Lichess the connections talk to.

next_event.description: The id the next event will get.

policy.description: Fair play: whether analysis is allowed now.

stopped.description: False when it had already ended.

Subject.description: What a piece of work is about, so the UI can link to it.

Symmetry.description: How symmetric the pairs of identical engines came out.

z_doubles.description: `(WW − LL) / √(WW + LL)`: how many standard errors the doubles lean towards the change.

z_halves.description: `(WD − LD) / √(WD + LD)`, the same for the half points.

Theme.description: What a drill is about: the opening family of its game, and the phase it came from.

oneOf.description: A clock per side and an increment per move.
Lichess's correspondence: days per move.
A fixed time per move, no clock.
A fixed number of nodes per move: no clock, so speed does not count, only search and evaluation.

TimeControl.description: How long each move may take.

TimeStats.description: Think time per move, from reviewed games with a clock (Lichess records no time for each side's first move).

time_trouble_blunders.description: Blunders played with less than a tenth of the starting clock left, in all and per game.

Timestamp.description:
A moment as an ISO-8601 UTC string, always written `2026-10-25T14:32:07.123Z` so they sort as text. `core` never
reads a clock: whoever makes one passes the time in (milliseconds since the epoch, or a string from Lichess or the
database).

token.description:
A personal Lichess token: yours with `board:play` (and `challenge:read`, `challenge:write`), the bot's with
`bot:play`.

TrainProgress.description:
`train.progress`: a training run's latest reading (throttled to one a second). Published on `idea:<id>` when the
run is a net idea's, else on `work`.

TrainSchedule.description: A run's schedule, as `bullet-train train` takes it.

final_wdl.description: ... and at the end (the same as `wdl` when left out).

wdl.description: The weight of the game result in the target, at the start.

TrainSpec.description: What a training run trains: the `Train` work's spec, and a `net` idea's `train`.

datasets.description: The data; empty means every dataset in Reckless's internal units.

from_scratch.description: Train from random weights instead of fine-tuning.

keep_checkpoints.description: Checkpoints kept, newest first (about 0.72 GB each).

name.description: The new net's name; `net-<work id>` when left out.

oneOf.description: The net to fine-tune; the champion's when left out (unless `from_scratch`).

save_rate.description: A checkpoint every this many superbatches (and at the end).

TrainStep.description: One reading of a run, as the loss chart plots it: kept for every `progress` line of the trainer.

loss.description: The mean batch loss since the previous reading.

seq.description: From 1, in the order the trainer wrote them.

TrainView.description: `GET /api/ideas/{id}/train`: a net idea's training: its settings, every reading so far and the net it made.

TrendPoint.description: One game on the trend line, oldest first.

accuracy.description: The player's accuracy in it, when reviewed.

points.description: 1, ½ or 0; none for an unfinished game.

rating.description: The player's rating in it, when known.

Trial.description: One stage of an idea: a set of games (or benches, or SPSA) and a verdict.

bounds.description: SPRT bounds in normalized Elo, `[lower, upper]`.

oneOf.description: Logistic Elo ± 95 %.

pairs.description: A fixed number of game pairs instead of an SPRT (a custom trial).

penta.description: Game pairs from the idea's side: `[LL, LD, DD+WL, WD, WW]`.

oneOf.description: The clock after scaling (11+0.11).
The clock as written (8+0.08).

wdl.description: Games won, drawn and lost by the idea's side.

idea.description: The trial's idea, which is the topic it is published on.

TrialSummary.description: What an idea shows of each trial.

Tunable.description: One tunable: its range and step sizes, and where it starts.

c_end.description: The perturbation at the last iteration.

r_end.description: The learning rate `a_k / c_k²` at the last iteration.

TunableOverride.description:
A parameter to tune, as asked: anything left out comes from the engine's declaration, so `{ "name": "x" }` tunes
`x` as declared.

params.description: The parameters, in the order of each step's values.

TuneParamInfo.description: A tuned parameter: its name, and its range when the tuned branch's `spsa` build is known.

iteration.description: Counted from 1, in the order updates were applied.

result.description: θ+'s games won minus games lost.

values.description: Every parameter after it, in the tune's order.

concurrency.description: Games at once; none for what the scheduler grants.

params.description: The parameters; empty means every declared tunable.

time.description: The games' clock as written (scaled when the tune starts), or a node limit.

TuneStep.description: One applied update: the store's `tune_steps` row.

iteration.description: Counted from 1, in the order updates were applied.

penta.description: θ+ against θ−, as game pairs from θ+'s side.

result.description: Games won minus games lost by θ+.

values.description: Every parameter after this step, in the order of the tune's parameters.

Version.description: One commit of Dameless that matters: the champion line, an idea's change, an upstream tip.

bench.description: The commit's `Bench:` line: the engine's functional fingerprint.

oneOf.description: Elo against its parent, from the deciding trial.

name.description: `v14` on the champion line, else the branch name.

oneOf.description:
The net its builds embed; none for the commit's own (the file its build script names). A version of the
champion's code with a trained net is named `v14 + net-3`, and a champion can be code plus a net.
The champion it was built on.

VersionId.description: A commit of Dameless that matters.

score.description: Points scored, as a percentage of the decided games.

WeakSpot.description: A position before one of the player's mistakes or blunders in a reviewed game, to play out again.

played.description: What was played, and what was better, in SAN.

recurring.description: How many weak spots share this one's opening family and phase: recurring themes come first.

paused_for.description: Why it is paused, for people: "Your Lichess game", "Live analysis".

WorkLists.description: The queue as people see it.

queued.description: In the order it will run.

WorkLog.description: `work.log`: one line of a work item's log.

YouSeek.description: Your seek in the lobby, open until someone takes it.

elsewhere.description: Your games on Lichess that cannot be played here.

seek_note.description: How the last seek went, for people.
